item.name: Five Tribes: Les Djinns de Naqala
item.originalname: Five Tribes: The Djinns of Naqala
item.comment:
Very clever game, everything is open, you try to optimize your strategy (often relying on an early Djinn acquisition) and it feels pleasant.
Not too many "in your face" moves and only a little player interaction through bids for turn order and obtaining djinns/items before others.
Works well with two with very combo-ish turns (you can have "double" turns).
This game is very prone to AP, I tend to recommend to analyze the board during other people's turn trying to find your best chance to earn VP's and when it's your turn, you only have to calculate how not to give too many options away.
A very refined game with several paths to victory (although you cannot neglect any).

item.comment: Favorite role-selection game (apart from Puerto rico). The "mandatory" Gathering Storm expansion gives you more routes to victory.

item.name: Race for the Galaxy: Tempête en formation
item.originalname: Race for the Galaxy: The Gathering Storm
item.comment:
If there's only one expansion to buy, it's this one. It adds new 6+ developpements and the "first player to ..." tiles that may give you an early game objective while waiting for a particular guild/card.
It adds to the game without trying to make it more than a card game (unlike other expansions, where you begin to have several tableau's to handle).

item.name: San Juan
item.comment: Great game to familiarize someone with role-picking games but often end up being shadowed by Race For The Galaxy (in my collection). Also, major concern here is that two of the buildings are mandatory for victory (without expansion of course). If your opponent has 1+ of them and you don't, goodbye victory. If all opponents know this, it becomes a race towards optimisation, but it circles around quickly.
